interactions.summary: Jiang keeps pressing the class for why God would grant agency at all, and the students answer with contrast, anti-blind-obedience, and cosmic-order models while he rejects easy experimental language.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led classroom exchange with several student replies

claims.claim: A student argues that genuine goodness requires a real possibility of evil, so willing the good only matters if humans could also choose otherwise.
Jiang restates that answer as a troubling model in which God would need evil in order to produce good, then asks whether a real God would operate that way at all.
One student tries a radical alternative by asking what happens if God did not create human beings at all, which Jiang immediately rejects by insisting that would negate God's divinity.
A student proposes that God does not want blind obedience, because forced belief would erase the meaningful relation between divinity and humanity.

Another student anchors the discussion in Dante's cosmology by saying natural things keep their ordained motion automatically, while human beings uniquely have the capacity to stray from their proper path.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang refuses to let a neat free-will answer stand until it survives the harder question of whether God would really engineer evil to manufacture good.
signature_moments.source_phrase: would God actually do any of this
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The packet is not just about doctrine; it shows Jiang using moral discomfort to test the coherence of theological models.

signature_moments.moment: Blind obedience appears as the opposite of what God wants from human creatures.
signature_moments.source_phrase: he doesn't want blind obedience from humanity
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This gives the class a sharp negative definition of agency: freedom matters because coerced belief would hollow out the relationship to God.

signature_moments.moment: The student turns Dante's ordered universe into a contrast between rocks and fire that obey automatically and humans who can wander off course.
signature_moments.source_phrase: rocks fall downward, the fire burns upwards
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It translates metaphysical order into memorable physical images and isolates free will as the strange human exception.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Used as the condition God supposedly does not want, because forced belief would empty human agency of meaning.
Dante's cosmic arrangement in which natural things follow their proper motion while humans can depart from it.
The distinctly human capacity Jiang keeps interrogating: the freedom to choose, stray, and therefore make goodness meaningful.

chronology_notes.note: This packet remains inside the same June 15 free-will discussion and does not introduce a dated change relative to another Jiang source.

uncertainty_notes.note: The seg-0132 exchange is clipped and compressed in ASR, but the core move is still legible as a student proposing a non-creation scenario that Jiang rejects.
